page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E4.Flex.8-128 is an x86_64 compute instance configured with 8 physical cores and 16 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 7J13 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.55 GHz. The instance features dedicated CPU core allocation with two hardware threads per physical core, complemented by 64 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. Memory is provisioned at 128.0 GB, yielding a high 1:8 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 8.0 GB per virtual processor. The instance does not include integrated local NVMe storage or discrete hardware acceleration GPUs, relying on remote block storage for persistence while providing one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core compute performance, with stress-ng recording 2687.18 operations. In multi-threaded evaluations, performance sits comfortably within the middle tier, yielding a Geekbench multi-core score of 9665.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 21085.5. Memory subsystem throughput shows balanced cached reads at 1026.81 GB/sec and uncached read bandwidth of 39.37 GB/sec, though large-block write bandwidth registers lower at 22.51 GB/sec. Application benchmarks indicate steady throughput for data serving and caching tiers, achieving 15.14 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 20.16 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

By delivering an expanded memory pool without demanding high core counts, VM.Standard.E4.Flex.8-128 optimizes infrastructure expenditure for memory-dense deployments. The absence of local solid-state drives necessitates external volume provisioning, representing a clear architectural tradeoff for disk-bound IOPS workloads. The configuration is primarily suited for in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, enterprise application servers, mid-tier relational database hosting, and memory-intensive ETL batch processing.

It provides 8 dedicated physical cores mapped to 16 vCPUs alongside 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding an expansive 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The server includes no onboard local storage and no GPU accelerators, using network block volumes for disk storage and supplying a single public IPv4 address. Benchmarks reveal strong single-thread CPU performance in stress-ng tests, alongside consistent mid-tier multi-threaded execution in Geekbench and PassMark. Cached memory reads are high, while uncached write operations reflect lower bandwidth throughput. This hardware distribution offers strong resource efficiency for memory-heavy operations, functioning well for in-memory caching solutions, mid-sized database management systems, and backend business logic deployments.
